html:
Francois Duvalier, called Papa Doc, was a country doctor elected president of Haiti in 1957, who made himself president for life in 1964 and ruled by terror until his death in 1971.

He built a militia, the Tonton Macoute, which killed and tortured opponents; tens of thousands died. He used the imagery of Vodou and of Black nationalism, and the United States backed him as an anti-communist during the Cold War.

Much of the educated class fled, beginning the large Haitian diaspora. His son Jean-Claude, Baby Doc, took over at 19 and ruled until a popular revolt drove him into exile in 1986. The return to elections led to Aristide.
